metadata.name: Autoimmune Disease-Gene Associations
metadata.description: Curated disease-gene associations for major autoimmune diseases, including pathogenic mechanisms, key cell types, HLA associations, autoantibodies, and approved therapies. Gene associations include GWAS hits, functional variants, and expression studies.

diseases.description: Chronic systemic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent synovitis, cartilage destruction, and bone erosion. Driven by aberrant T cell and B cell activation, pro-inflammatory cytokine networks (TNF, IL-6, IL-1), and autoantibody production (RF, ACPA). Affects approximately 0.5-1% of the global population with a female predominance.
pathogenic_mechanisms: Citrullination and ACPA-mediated immune complex formation

associated_genes.description: Shared epitope alleles confer strongest genetic risk for seropositive RA
R620W variant alters T cell receptor signaling threshold and B cell autoreactivity
Risk alleles enhance IFN-gamma and IL-12 signaling in T cells
Polymorphisms reduce co-inhibitory signaling, promoting T cell activation
Modulates TNF receptor signaling and complement activation
Chemokine receptor involved in Th17 cell migration to inflamed synovium
Encodes gp130 subunit of IL-6 receptor complex; critical for IL-6 trans-signaling
Co-stimulatory molecule essential for B cell activation and germinal center formation
Peptidylarginine deiminase 4 catalyzes citrullination of proteins, generating ACPA targets
CD25 variant affects regulatory T cell homeostasis

diseases.description: Multi-organ autoimmune disease characterized by loss of self-tolerance, autoantibody production (anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith), immune complex deposition, and type I interferon dysregulation. Affects skin, joints, kidneys, CNS, and blood. Predominantly affects women of childbearing age with strong genetic and environmental contributions.
pathogenic_mechanisms: Type I interferon overproduction and ISG signature
Immune complex deposition in kidneys and vasculature
Loss of B cell tolerance and plasmablast expansion
NETosis and neutrophil extracellular trap pathology
key_cell_types: Autoreactive B cells and plasma cells

associated_genes.description: Multiple alleles confer risk for lupus, especially DRB1*03:01 and DRB1*15:01
Transcription factor critical for type I IFN production; risk haplotype increases expression
Mediates IL-12 and IFN-alpha signaling; risk allele enhances Th1 responses
Encodes CD11b (complement receptor 3); variants impair immune complex clearance
Encodes A20 ubiquitin-editing enzyme; loss of function amplifies NF-κB signaling
B lymphocyte kinase involved in B cell receptor signaling
OX40L co-stimulatory molecule promotes T cell-B cell interactions
R620W variant affects lymphocyte signaling threshold
Homozygous C1q deficiency causes lupus in >90% of cases; impairs apoptotic cell clearance
Exonuclease mutations cause Aicardi-Goutières and lupus-like syndromes via cytosolic DNA accumulation

diseases.description: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating disease of the central nervous system. Autoreactive T cells cross the blood-brain barrier and attack myelin sheaths, leading to axonal damage and neurodegeneration. Characterized by relapsing-remitting or progressive courses with focal white matter lesions on MRI.
pathogenic_mechanisms: Blood-brain barrier breakdown and immune cell infiltration
Th1 and Th17 cell-mediated myelin destruction
B cell-derived meningeal ectopic lymphoid tissue

associated_genes.description: DRB1*15:01 is the strongest genetic risk factor for MS, presenting myelin peptides to CD4+ T cells
CD25 variant affects Treg function and IL-2 signaling
Encodes IL-7 receptor alpha; variant alters T cell homeostasis and survival
LFA-3 ligand for CD2; modulates T cell activation and NK cell function
Involved in autophagy and thymic selection; risk variant may impair central tolerance
Cell cycle regulator; risk variant linked to T cell proliferation dysregulation
JAK family kinase mediating IFN and IL-12 signaling; protective variants reduce kinase activity
Risk variant increases CD40 expression on antigen-presenting cells

diseases.description: Organ-specific autoimmune disease resulting from T cell-mediated destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic beta cells. Characterized by progressive loss of beta cell mass leading to absolute insulin deficiency. Involves genetic susceptibility (HLA-DR/DQ), environmental triggers, and islet autoantibodies that predict disease onset.
diseases.prevalence: 15-30 per 100,000 per year (incidence); varies by geography
pathogenic_mechanisms: CD8+ T cell-mediated beta cell killing
Loss of peripheral and central tolerance to islet autoantigens
Beta cell ER stress and unfolded protein response
Defective Treg function in pancreatic lymph nodes

associated_genes.description: DQB1*03:02 and DQB1*02:01 confer highest risk; DQB1*06:02 is strongly protective
DR3-DQ2 and DR4-DQ8 haplotypes account for ~50% of genetic risk
Variable number tandem repeat (VNTR) in insulin gene promoter affects thymic insulin expression and central tolerance
R620W variant affects T cell receptor signaling and negative selection
Reduced inhibitory co-stimulation promotes autoreactive T cell activation
CD25 variants impair Treg development and IL-2 signaling
Receptor tyrosine kinase involved in beta cell regeneration
LNK adaptor protein negatively regulates cytokine signaling; risk variant increases inflammatory responses

diseases.description: Chronic inflammatory conditions of the gastrointestinal tract encompassing Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. Driven by dysregulated mucosal immune responses to gut microbiota in genetically susceptible individuals. Involves barrier dysfunction, innate and adaptive immune activation, and tissue remodeling.
diseases.prevalence: 0.3-0.5% in Western countries; rising incidence globally
pathogenic_mechanisms: Intestinal barrier dysfunction and increased permeability
Dysbiosis and aberrant immune response to commensal bacteria
TNF and IL-23/IL-17 axis-driven mucosal inflammation
Defective autophagy and intracellular bacterial handling

associated_genes.description: Intracellular pattern recognition receptor for muramyl dipeptide; three coding variants (R702W, G908R, L1007fs) confer risk for Crohn's disease
Autophagy gene; T300A variant impairs xenophagy and Paneth cell function
IL-23 receptor variant modulates Th17 responses; protective R381Q variant
Immunity-related GTPase involved in autophagy of intracellular bacteria
Multiple HLA alleles contribute to UC and CD susceptibility
Anti-inflammatory cytokine; rare mutations cause very early-onset IBD
Leucine-rich repeat kinase shared risk locus with Parkinson's disease; involved in autophagy and inflammation
NF-κB activator downstream of innate immune receptors; variant affects antifungal immunity

diseases.description: Chronic immune-mediated skin disease driven by the IL-23/IL-17 axis, resulting in keratinocyte hyperproliferation, epidermal thickening, and characteristic scaly plaques. Associated with psoriatic arthritis, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic syndrome. Involves complex interactions between dendritic cells, T cells, and keratinocytes.
pathogenic_mechanisms: Dendritic cell activation and TNF/IL-23 production
Th17 and Tc17 cell accumulation in skin

associated_genes.description: HLA-C*06:02 (PSORS1) is the strongest genetic determinant, presenting LL37 peptides to CD8+ T cells
Encodes p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23; risk variant increases IL-23 production
IL-23 receptor variant enhances Th17 differentiation and IL-17 production
A20 deubiquitinase; loss-of-function variants enhance NF-κB activity
A20-binding inhibitor of NF-κB; variant reduces inhibitory function
Encodes p19 subunit of IL-23
ACT1 adaptor protein mediating IL-17 receptor signaling; D10N variant alters NF-κB activation
Inducible nitric oxide synthase; involved in keratinocyte inflammatory response

diseases.description: Chronic inflammatory disease primarily affecting the axial skeleton and sacroiliac joints, characterized by enthesitis, new bone formation, and progressive spinal fusion (bamboo spine). Part of the spondyloarthritis spectrum. Unique pathology involves IL-17/IL-23 axis, mechanical stress responses, and aberrant osteoblast activation at entheseal sites.
pathogenic_mechanisms: HLA-B27 misfolding and unfolded protein response
Aberrant bone formation via Wnt signaling
Innate immune activation (ILC3, gamma-delta T cells)

associated_genes.description: HLA-B*27 present in >90% of patients; misfolding triggers UPR and IL-23 production
IL-23 receptor; protective R381Q variant reduces Th17 differentiation
Aminopeptidase that trims peptides for HLA-B27 loading; epistatic interaction with HLA-B27
Decoy receptor for IL-1; variant affects IL-1 signaling intensity
Transcription factor involved in CD8+ T cell and ILC3 development
JAK family kinase downstream of IL-23R; protective variants reduce kinase activity
Lymphotoxin beta receptor involved in lymphoid tissue organogenesis

diseases.description: Chronic autoimmune disease targeting exocrine glands (salivary and lacrimal), causing sicca symptoms (dry eyes and mouth). Characterized by lymphocytic infiltration of glands, B cell hyperactivity, and risk of B cell lymphoma. Can occur as primary disease or secondary to other autoimmune conditions.
pathogenic_mechanisms: Ectopic germinal center formation in salivary glands
BAFF/BLyS overexpression promoting B cell survival
key_cell_types: Epithelial cells (both target and antigen presenter)

associated_genes.description: DRB1*03:01 is strongly associated with anti-Ro/SSA positive Sjögren's
Interferon regulatory factor; risk haplotype enhances type I IFN production
Mediates IFN-alpha and IL-12 signaling
B lymphocyte kinase; risk variant affects B cell receptor signaling
A20 ubiquitin editor; variants amplify NF-κB signaling
Chemokine receptor for follicular homing; involved in ectopic GC formation
OX40L co-stimulatory molecule promoting T-B cell interaction

diseases.description: Complex autoimmune disease characterized by vasculopathy, immune activation, and progressive fibrosis of skin and internal organs. Early vascular injury triggers immune activation and fibroblast differentiation to myofibroblasts, leading to excessive extracellular matrix deposition. Classified as limited cutaneous (lcSSc) or diffuse cutaneous (dcSSc) subtypes.
pathogenic_mechanisms: Complement and immune complex-mediated vascular damage

associated_genes.description: DRB1*11:04 associated with anti-topoisomerase I (dcSSc); DRB1*01:04 with anti-centromere (lcSSc)
Interferon regulatory factor; risk variant enhances type I IFN and inflammatory cytokine production
Transcription factor mediating IFN and IL-12 signaling
B cell scaffold protein; risk variant affects B cell receptor signaling
OX40L co-stimulatory molecule
CD3 zeta chain of TCR complex; variant affects T cell activation
Connective tissue growth factor; overexpressed in SSc fibroblasts, mediates TGF-β profibrotic effects

diseases.description: Antibody-mediated autoimmune disease of the neuromuscular junction. Autoantibodies against acetylcholine receptors (AChR), muscle-specific kinase (MuSK), or LRP4 impair neuromuscular transmission, causing fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness and fatigability. Thymic abnormalities (thymoma, thymic hyperplasia) are common.
pathogenic_mechanisms: Anti-AChR antibody-mediated complement activation at NMJ
Blockade of AChR ligand binding site
Anti-MuSK antibody disruption of AChR clustering
Thymic B cell activation and ectopic germinal centers
key_cell_types: B cells and plasma cells (autoantibody source)

associated_genes.description: DRB1*03:01 associated with early-onset AChR+ MG; DRB1*14 with MuSK+ MG
Encodes AChR alpha subunit; primary autoantigen in ~85% of patients
Muscle-specific kinase; autoantigen in ~5-10% of MG patients (AChR-negative)
T cell co-inhibitory receptor; variant affects peripheral tolerance
Lymphocyte phosphatase affecting signaling threshold
RANK receptor; variant may influence thymic development

diseases.description: Group of necrotizing small-vessel vasculitides including granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), microscopic polyangiitis (MPA), and eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA). ANCA autoantibodies (PR3-ANCA or MPO-ANCA) activate neutrophils, causing endothelial damage and organ involvement (kidneys, lungs, ENT).
key_cell_types: B cells and plasma cells (ANCA source)

associated_genes.description: DPB1*04:01 strongly associated with PR3-ANCA/GPA
Encodes alpha-1 antitrypsin (PR3 inhibitor); Z allele increases GPA risk by impairing PR3 neutralization
Encodes proteinase 3 (PR3); expression level on neutrophils correlates with disease activity
Associations with MPO-ANCA subtype
T cell co-inhibitory receptor variant
R620W variant affects lymphocyte signaling; associated with GPA

diseases.description: Immune-mediated enteropathy triggered by dietary gluten in genetically susceptible individuals (HLA-DQ2/DQ8). Tissue transglutaminase (tTG) deamidates gliadin peptides, creating high-affinity HLA-DQ2/DQ8 ligands that activate CD4+ T cells, driving villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, and intraepithelial lymphocytosis.
pathogenic_mechanisms: Gliadin peptide deamidation by tissue transglutaminase
IL-15-driven intraepithelial cytotoxic T cell expansion
key_cell_types: B cells and plasma cells (anti-tTG source)

associated_genes.description: HLA-DQ2.5 (DQA1*05:01/DQB1*02:01) present in ~90% of patients; HLA-DQ8 in most remaining cases
Shared locus affecting T cell proliferation and differentiation
LNK adaptor protein; risk variant increases T cell activation
Chemokine receptor involved in immune cell recruitment to gut
IL-18 receptor accessory protein; IL-18 drives IFN-gamma production by intraepithelial lymphocytes
Regulator of G-protein signaling; affects T cell homing to gut
Tissue transglutaminase 2; deamidates gliadin peptides and is the primary autoantigen

diseases.description: Chronic immune-mediated inflammatory arthritis associated with psoriasis and part of the seronegative spondyloarthritis spectrum. Heterogeneous presentation spanning peripheral arthritis, axial disease, enthesitis, dactylitis, and nail involvement. Pathology centers on the IL-23/IL-17 axis and TNF-alpha, with enthesitis as the primary lesion. Develops in roughly 20-30% of psoriasis patients and is characteristically seronegative for rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP.
diseases.prevalence: 0.1-0.25% of the general population; arises in ~20-30% of psoriasis patients; male:female ratio ~1:1
pathogenic_mechanisms: IL-23/IL-17 axis driving enthesitis and synovitis
TNF-alpha-driven synovial inflammation and joint destruction
Enthesitis as the primary lesion (entheseal resident IL-23R+ cells)
Dysregulated osteoproliferation (new bone formation) alongside osteoclast-mediated erosion
Skin-joint axis of shared psoriatic inflammation
Innate and innate-like immune activation (gamma-delta T cells, ILC3, MAIT cells)
Gut-joint axis with subclinical bowel inflammation and dysbiosis

associated_genes.description: HLA-C*06:02 is the major psoriasis risk allele; associated with earlier skin onset and the cutaneous-predominant psoriatic arthritis phenotype
HLA-B*27 (axial disease), B*08, B*38 and B*39 associate with distinct articular and peripheral phenotypes
IL-23 receptor; protective R381Q variant dampens Th17 differentiation and IL-17 production
Encodes the p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23; central to the IL-23/IL-17 axis
Encodes the IL-23-specific p19 subunit driving maintenance of pathogenic Th17 cells
Encodes the Act1 adaptor that transduces IL-17 receptor signaling; risk variant links skin and joint disease
TNFAIP3-interacting protein 1; negative regulator of NF-kB downstream of TNF
JAK-family kinase downstream of IL-23R and IL-12; protective loss-of-function variants reduce signaling
ER aminopeptidase trimming peptides for MHC-I loading; epistatic interaction with HLA-B*27 and HLA-C*06
c-Rel NF-kB subunit; risk locus shared across psoriatic and other immune-mediated disease
